# onetsolutions_instance_firewall (Resource)

Manages the customer firewall rules of an instance.

The resource is authoritative over the customer rules: a rule created outside Terraform is removed
on the next apply, and a rule deleted outside Terraform is recreated. Rules are matched by `name`,
so names must be unique.

**Platform-managed rules are never touched.** The rules OnetSolutions keeps on an instance — those
whose source is a platform address (such as `Control Plane`) and those whose name starts with
`One Click Apps · ` or `one-click:` (installed by One Click Apps) — are not read into the state,
not reported as drift, and neither changed nor deleted, including on destroy.

The firewall is applied to the instance after every rule change, and the next change waits until
that application ends, up to the timeout: each changed rule costs one application. Destroying the
resource deletes the customer rules and waits for the firewall to be applied again. Once the
instance is cancelled or terminated, its rules can no longer be changed: the next refresh removes
this resource from the state, and destroying it succeeds without a change.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The customer rules of the instance. Platform-managed rules (control-plane access, One Click
# Apps) stay in place and are never listed here.
resource "onetsolutions_instance_firewall" "web" {
  instance_id = onetsolutions_instance.web.id

  rule {
    name             = "ssh-office"
    description      = "SSH from the office only"
    direction        = "inbound"
    action           = "accept"
    protocol         = "tcp"
    source_cidr      = "198.51.100.0/24"
    destination_port = "22"
    priority         = 100
  }

  rule {
    name             = "web"
    direction        = "inbound"
    action           = "accept"
    protocol         = "tcp"
    destination_port = "80,443"
    priority         = 200
  }

  rule {
    name      = "no-ping"
    direction = "inbound"
    action    = "drop"
    protocol  = "icmp"
    priority  = 300
  }

  timeouts {
    update = "15m"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The UUID of the instance. Changing it moves the rules to another instance (replacement).

### Optional

- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `rule` (Block List) A customer rule. Omit every `rule` block to keep no customer rule at all. After an import the rules are read in priority order: list them in that order to avoid a reorder-only change. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule))
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The UUID of the instance: an instance has one firewall.

<a id="nestedblock--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `action` (String) What the rule does with matching traffic: `accept`, `drop` or `reject`.
- `direction` (String) The traffic the rule applies to: `inbound` or `outbound`.
- `name` (String) The name of the rule, unique among the instance's rules: rules are matched by name. It must not start with `One Click Apps · ` or `one-click:`, which name platform rules.
- `priority` (Number) The order in which rules are evaluated, from 1 to 10000: the lowest first.
- `protocol` (String) The protocol matched: `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp` or `all`.

Optional:

- `description` (String) A free-form description of the rule. Defaults to an empty string.
- `destination_cidr` (String) The destination network in CIDR notation. When unset, matches any destination.
- `destination_port` (String) The destination ports: a port (`443`), a range (`1000-2000`) or a comma-separated list of both. Only for `tcp` and `udp`; unset matches every port.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is in force. Defaults to `true`.
- `source_cidr` (String) The source network in CIDR notation, such as `203.0.113.0/24`. Defaults to `0.0.0.0/0` (any source). A rule whose source is a platform address becomes platform-managed and is refused.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to wait for the creation, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `10m`.
- `delete` (String) How long to wait for the deletion, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `10m`.
- `update` (String) How long to wait for the update, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `10m`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_instance_firewall.web
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<instance_id>, or <instance_id> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
terraform import onetsolutions_instance_firewall.web 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d
```
